# `ceangal.widgets`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py from ceangal/src/widgets.almd; do not edit. -->

_Standard controls: buttons, checkboxes, switches, sliders, dialogs…._

Standard controls on top of ceangal.view: buttons, checkboxes, switches,
radio groups, segmented controls, dropdowns, menus, sliders, progress
bars, text fields, cards, list rows and dialogs, styled by one Theme.

  import ceangal.widgets as w
  let th = w.system()       // light or dark, following the system
  w.button(th, "Save", () => save())
  w.checkbox(th, "Remember me", remember, (on) => set_remember(on))

Every control is keyboard- and screen-reader-ready: it is a Tab stop
(Enter or Space activates it, arrows move a slider), has the right
role, label and state for assistive technology, shows a focus ring, and
reacts to hover and press. A control's key, which focus and hover go
by, comes from its label, so give the controls on one screen distinct
labels (which screen readers need anyway: "Remove Milk", not "Remove").

Controls hold no state: pass the current value in and change it in the
callback, as with everything else in a view.

```almide
import ceangal.widgets
```

### `Theme`

```almide
type Theme = {
  bg: snaidhm.Color,        // the window
  surface: snaidhm.Color,   // cards, fields, inactive controls
  raised: snaidhm.Color,    // hovered surfaces, tracks
  text: snaidhm.Color,
  dim: snaidhm.Color,       // secondary text, placeholders
  accent: snaidhm.Color,    // primary buttons, checked controls, links
  on_accent: snaidhm.Color, // text on the accent
  border: snaidhm.Color,
  focus: snaidhm.Color,     // the keyboard focus ring
  danger: snaidhm.Color,
  radius: Float,
  font_size: Float,
  editor: ed.Theme,         // text fields
}
```

### `dark`

```almide
pub fn dark() -> Theme
```

Dark surfaces, light text (the playground's dark palette).

### `light`

```almide
pub fn light() -> Theme
```

Light surfaces, dark text.

### `system`

```almide
pub fn system() -> Theme
```

dark() or light(), as the system's appearance is now (it can change while
the app runs; build the theme in view() so it follows).

### `mix`

```almide
pub fn mix(a: snaidhm.Color, b: snaidhm.Color, t: Float) -> snaidhm.Color
```

`a` moved toward `b` by t (0–1).

## Text

### `title`

```almide
pub fn title(th: Theme, s: String) -> v.View
```

A screen's title: large, bold, announced as a heading.

### `tooltip`

```almide
pub fn tooltip(th: Theme, text: String, control: v.View) -> v.View
```

`control` (which needs a key, as every control has) with a tooltip:
`text` in a bubble under it while the pointer rests on it or the
keyboard has focused it. Screen readers get the text as a tooltip
(role 28) while it shows.

### `heading`

```almide
pub fn heading(th: Theme, s: String) -> v.View
```

A section's heading.

### `body`

```almide
pub fn body(th: Theme, s: String) -> v.View
```

Ordinary text at the theme's size.

### `caption`

```almide
pub fn caption(th: Theme, s: String) -> v.View
```

Secondary text: hints, counts, timestamps.

### `link`

```almide
pub fn link(th: Theme, s: String, url: String) -> v.View
```

Text that opens `url` in the browser.

## Popups: dropdowns and menus

### `dropdown`

```almide
pub fn dropdown(th: Theme, label: String, options: List[String], index: Int, on_select: (Int) -> Unit) -> v.View
```

One choice out of a list, shown as the current one; the list opens under
it. Keyboard: Enter, Space or Alt+Down opens it, Up / Down then move and
Enter picks; while it is closed, Up / Down change the choice directly.

### `menu_button`

```almide
pub fn menu_button(th: Theme, title: String, items: List[(String, () -> Unit)]) -> v.View
```

A button that opens a menu of actions under it: each entry a title and
what it does. Keyboard as for a dropdown.

## Values

### `slider`

```almide
pub fn slider(th: Theme, label: String, value: Float, lo: Float, hi: Float, step: Float, on_change: (Float) -> Unit) -> v.View
```

A value from `lo` to `hi` (in steps of `step`; 0 = any). Drag or tap the
track; with focus, Left / Right (and a screen reader's adjust gesture)
move it a step (a twentieth of the range when step is 0).

### `progress`

```almide
pub fn progress(th: Theme, label: String, fraction: Float) -> v.View
```

How far a task has got: `fraction` from 0 to 1.

## Text entry

### `text_field`

```almide
pub fn text_field(th: Theme, key: String, label: String, get: () -> ed.Editor, set: (ed.Editor) -> Unit) -> v.View
```

A one-line text field: `get` / `set` hold its ed.Editor (make one with
ed.text_field(text, placeholder)). `label` is what a screen reader says.
(The editor paints its whole rect, so the border is on a box around it.)

### `dialog`

```almide
pub fn dialog(th: Theme, base: v.View, title: String, content: List[v.View], actions: List[v.View], on_dismiss: () -> Unit) -> v.View
```

A dialog over `base`: a dimmed backdrop (clicking it calls `on_dismiss`)
and a card with a title, content and a row of actions. Show it by
returning `dialog(...)` from view() while it is open, `base` otherwise:

  fn view() -> v.View = if confirming then w.dialog(th, page(), "Delete?", [w.body(th, "…")],
    [w.secondary_button(th, "Cancel", () => close()), w.danger_button(th, "Delete", () => delete())], () => close())
    else page()

Escape is the app's to handle (ceangal.on_key), as it may mean more than
closing the dialog.
